quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What is required for footrests on a motorcycle?

options.text: They can be shared by the driver and passenger.
They are required for both the driver and passenger.
They are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing helps keep your passenger from falling off and pulling you with them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends.
The left lane ends.
A traffic control device is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden movements when possible.
Handle your motorcycle roughly.
Use only your front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements when possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps in the road ahead?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper and see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: At night, watch the vehicle ahead to know about road conditions. Its headlights may light up the road better than yours. If the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like car mirrors.
No, they do not have blind spots.
Mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from learning to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What type of gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Half-fingered gloves
Full-fingered gloves
You should not wear gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands while riding. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you avoid?

options.text: Using the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Using the front brake because it can cause the bike to tip over.
Using the front brake to increase stability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the front brake because it can cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed during the turn.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT a benefit of keeping a space cushion between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: A space cushion around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: There is an oily strip in the center of a lane. What does this strip do?

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually gives good grip for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good grip for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually gives enough grip for safe riding, unless it is raining. The strip is usually less than two feet wide. You can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves again.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you approach the emergency scene.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, do NOT:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you are doing by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to match the situation. Change your lane position or direction as needed to stay safe.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Press your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: In normal conditions, how far behind another vehicle should a motorcycle stay?

options.text: At least two seconds.
At least three seconds.
At least four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. When conditions are bad, stay even farther back.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is clear pavement that is at least eight feet wide to the right of the other vehicle. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: In areas where dangers could happen, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep the same speed.
Assume they will be safe.
Cover the clutch and both brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brakes to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brakes so you can react faster in an emergency.

questions.question: What is one way to help prevent a crash?

options.text: Don't use turn signals.
Use the correct lane position.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct lane position.
questions.explanation: To help prevent crashes, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep safe distance, look 12 seconds ahead, spot hazards early, and be ready for changes.

questions.question: In normal riding conditions, what is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on, along with your running lights if you have them. Use your high beam both day and night when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Only in emergencies.
Together with the rear brake.
It is not safe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT recommended protective clothing for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Long pants
Gloves
A baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good choices include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
On the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding too far away may encourage them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid areas with heavy traffic.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road well ahead of your motorcycle to avoid dangerous situations. Watch for potential hazards and react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull over and wait until it stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of a lane becomes slippery with oil. Stay safe by riding in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is usually safest, but this can change.

questions.question: When shifting gears while turning a curve, what is best?

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
Shifting during a curve is better than before it.
It is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can make the rear wheel skid.
